Main cultivated crops of this zone: potato, maize,beans and peas.

Population increases have resulted in pressure on the land, resulting in cultivation of small plots for most farmers. The soils of the Central Plateau have a high potential for a wide range of crops. Crop cultivation on the Granitic Ridge is mainly concentrated on the concave hillslopes, while the convex ridges are used for pasture and forest. In the Southeast, the soils are strongly variable, with humus-rich, gravelly soils on the upper slopes and more fertile and younger soils on the foot of the hillslopes. Slope gradients increase significantly in the South, where forestry is the only advised land use. Moderately deep soils. Main limitations are erosion risks and low water availability. Management for erosion prevention is usually required. Most important crops: sorghum, sweet potato, cassava and beans.

Driest region of Rwanda, especially Eastern Savanna and central Bugesera. Eastern Savanna is mostly used for pasture. Main limiting factors are lack of rainfall and long dry seasons. Varying land use potentials, where the most suitable cropland is found in the eastern valleys and around the Muhazi lake. Careful management to prevent erosion and restore soil nutrient balance is required to ensure sustainable crop production. Irrigation techniques due to long dry season are necessary and drainage systems are required in valleys with poor drainage. Intercropping is a common practice. Most important crops: banana, cassava, beans and maize.
